column3: The Hebrew specifically describes residing as a sojourner with Laban.
The Hebrew says “he said,” rather than “he thought.”
The Hebrew says “I will do good with you,” rather than the more specific “make you prosper.”
The Hebrew says “with my staff” without an explicit “only,” and calls the river “this Jordan.”
The Hebrew repeats “from the hand”: “from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau.” It has “mother with children,” with “mother” singular.
The Hebrew says “I will surely do good with you,” rather than specifically “make you prosper.”
The Hebrew says “from what came into his hand,” rather than explicitly what he had brought with him.
The Hebrew preserves the image of giving the animals “into the hand” of his servants.
The Hebrew says “he too is behind us,” without repeating Jacob’s name.
The Hebrew repeatedly uses “face”: appeasing his face, seeing his face, and perhaps his lifting Jacob’s face.
The Hebrew has “the gift,” singular, and says it passed before his face.
The Hebrew uses the broader word “children,” rather than specifically “sons.”
The Hebrew repeats the action of sending across for the people and the possessions.
The Hebrew says “touched” the hip socket, then describes its being dislocated, rather than directly saying he struck and dislocated it.
